display: Phuket — eastern pier arc (Rassada / Bang Rong / Ao Po / Chalong)
summary: Phuket's east coast holds its working marine gateways: Rassada (the island's main ferry hub to Phi Phi/Krabi), Bang Rong and Ao Po (gateways to Phang Nga Bay and the Yao islands), and Chalong in the south (dive and island-day-trip launch). These existing multi-operator piers are the natural pedestal sites and the spine of a Thailand-clean Phuket/Andaman market, separated from the older Phuket+Malaysia bundle.

micro_demand: Rassada is the highest-throughput Andaman ferry node — captive transfer demand to Phi Phi/Krabi.
Bang Rong / Ao Po feed Phang Nga Bay and Koh Yao Noi/Yai — premium and commuter mix.
Chalong concentrates dive-boat and southern-island day-trip launches.
navier_fit: High. Established multi-operator piers ease pedestal siting; mix of captive island transfers and premium bay tours within Pioneer II range. Cross-corridors (Phuket<->Krabi, Phuket<->Phi Phi) need monsoon range-gating.

grab_overlay.super_app_fit: Grab in-app island-transfer + bay-tour booking with GrabCar pier handoff at Rassada and Chalong.
grab_overlay.wedge: Anchor a Thailand-clean Phuket/Andaman offer on Rassada throughput; pre-booked electric lane for the Phi Phi corridor.
